definition.text: The junction between the axon of a motor neuron and a muscle fiber. In response to the arrival of action potentials, the presynaptic button releases molecules of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. These diffuse across the cleft and transmit the signal to the postsynaptic membrane of the muscle fiber, leading to a change in post-synaptic potential.

description.text:
The receptors are composed of varying numbers and types of subunit. Each subunit contains a large extracellular N-terminal ligand-binding region; 3 hydrophobic transmembrane domains; a large intracellular region; and a fourth hydrophobic domain. The GABA, acetylcholine, serotonin 5HT3 and glycine receptors share a degree of sequence similarity, but differ from the glutamate receptors - sequences of this family possess 2 Cys residues in the N-terminal domain, which, in nicotinic receptors, form a disulphide bond essential for correct folding of the structure [[cite:PUB00087336]].

This entry includes the subunits of the GABA-A, nicotinic, glycine, glutamate and 5HT3 receptors.

Neurotransmitter ligand-gated ion channels are transmembrane receptor-ion channel complexes that open transiently upon binding of specific ligands, allowing rapid transmission of signals at chemical synapses [[cite:PUB00002675], [cite:PUB00003455]]. Five of these ion channel receptor families have been shown to form a sequence-related superfamily:

  • Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (AchR), an excitatory cation channel in vertebrates and invertebrates; in vertebrate motor endplates it is composed of alpha, beta, gamma and delta/epsilon subunits; in neurons it is composed of alpha and non-alpha (or beta) subunits [[cite:PUB00044612]].
  • Glycine receptor, an inhibitory chloride ion channel composed of alpha and beta subunits [[cite:PUB00044613]].
  • Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptor, an inhibitory chloride ion channel; at least four types of subunits (alpha, beta, gamma and delta) are known [[cite:PUB00044614]].
  • Serotonin 5HT3 receptor, of which there are seven major types (5HT3-5HT7) [[cite:PUB00010340]].
  • Glutamate receptor, an excitatory cation channel of which at least three types have been described (kainate, N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) and quisqualate) [[cite:PUB00044615]].

These receptors possess a pentameric structure (made up of varying subunits), surrounding a central pore. All known sequences of subunits from neurotransmitter-gated ion-channels are structurally related. They are composed of a large extracellular glycosylated N-terminal ligand-binding domain, followed by three hydrophobic transmembrane regions which form the ionic channel, followed by an intracellular region of variable length. A fourth hydrophobic region is found at the C-terminal of the sequence [[cite:PUB00002675], [cite:PUB00003455]].

hpa.scope: Two actual target-channel images inspected; compartment corroboration, not evidence of receptor assembly or electrophysiology.

12928480: Exact normal abstract preserved; authentic indexed author-uploaded original Results/Fig.1 and Methods recovered. Intact-cell toxin binding and delta-antibody detection concern assembled receptor in HEK cells; no isolated-alpha microscopy or all-product equivalence claimed.
Reconstituted receptors containing wild-type or mutant alpha are measured on the cell surface.
15701510: Authentic original MRC-hosted PDF recovered and selected structural Results/Methods read. The approximately4-Angstrom helical membrane model is Torpedo marmorata, not human; independent human primary assays corroborate complex membership.
The alpha-containing heteropentamer provides intersubunit ligand interfaces and a shared transmembrane pore.
18252226: Full selected original Results/Discussion and expression Methods read. Human recessive genotypes, fetal reduced-muscle-mass phenotypes and mouse somite expression are distinct; therapeutic rescue belongs to RAPSN, not CHRNA1.

Severe human CHRNA1 defects associate with fetal akinesia and reduced muscle mass; a direct growth step is not resolved from impaired movement, and the proposed early mesodermal role remains speculative.
21480901: Authentic abstract explicitly identifies Torpedo receptors transplanted into Xenopus oocytes. Full original body was not recovered; no specific human construct or lidocaine-metabolism claim is made.
Acetylcholine-evoked receptor currents are inhibited by lidocaine in the tested transplanted-receptor system.
27375219: Full selected Methods37/40 and Results/Discussion78 inspected. The human subunit expression system and engineered alphaV255A experiment are explicit despite title emphasis on other subunits. Mature-chain numbering is distinguished from HGVS full-length numbering.
Human alpha-subunit pore residues contribute to receptor gating; intact-cell measurements establish surface expression.
7619526: Authenticated original abstract inspected; full original Methods not recovered. AlphaG153S human disease and altered agonist affinity are explicit, but exact construct origin is not inferred from the HEK host.
The alphaG153S variant alters agonist affinity and channel opening in slow-channel myasthenia.
8872460: Exact normal abstract remains unchanged. Authentic indexed author-uploaded original Results/Discussion/Methods recovered: human patient muscle recordings are distinct from recombinant mouse subunits in HEK cells. No full figure-pixel inspection claimed.
AlphaN217K changes channel behavior; the measured human injury and electrical failure are at muscle endplates, supporting muscle-specific source refinements.
9221765: Full original human muscle/endplate Methods and human-subunit HEK reconstitution Results read. Normal quantal release, altered channel kinetics, junctional-fold degeneration and mixed wild-type/mutant model limits are preserved.
Human alphaV249F increases activation/desensitization and agonist affinity, prolonging endplate responses and causing postsynaptic injury.
9546329: Authentic abstract of the six-patient open-label quinidine study inspected. Full body and per-patient gene assignments were not recovered; clinical improvement is not attributed solely to CHRNA1 or a drug-metabolizing activity.
Slow-channel syndrome treatment can improve muscle strength and compound muscle electrophysiology.
8788941: Genuine normal abstract and current UniProt product annotations inspected. Publisher/PMC full recovery failed; detailed Methods are not claimed. The abstract explicitly distinguishes human alpha from P3A-containing alpha+ in Xenopus oocytes.
The alpha+ product was not incorporated into functional receptors in the tested expression system.
16527851: Genuine normal full selected Methods21/22/29, Results40/49/52/54/55 and Discussion59/60 read. Human adult/fetal subunit combinations in rat GH4C1 cells are distinguished from primary human fetal-type myotubes and mouse controls.
Alpha1-containing human receptors conduct calcium; epsilon largely explains the high adult calcium fraction, while the tested alpha disease mutations do not change that fraction.

provider_attempt.result: Genuine Falcon timeout and fallback quota failure; no fabricated provider report.

product_scope: Original P02708-2 and P02708-1 identifiers/names remain exact, including their nonintuitive numbering. Normal human alpha function is not assigned equally to P3A-containing alpha+.

donor_extract.scope: Exact current identities/GOA rows; no historical PAINT IBD placement, MSA or gain/loss reconstruction. MGI/RGD direct queries returned400, not biological negatives. UniProt cross-references resolve their identities.

bounded_peer.scope: 14-row independent primary/ontology consultation, including 45 scoped donor records resolved through official UniProt cross-reference identities. Historical PAINT not reconstructed.
